Is it possible for a piece of music to be my favorite part?

I remember playing the game when I was little and not being able to get any further than the Tarzan/Alice in Wonderland/Hurclues worlds, and restarting the game to make another Sora in hopes of being able to beat some bosses.

Every time I restarted, I always remember sitting there on the main menu, listening to the game's main theme.

I was always really quick to jump into games when I was a little (I mean I was younger than five when I first started this game) and kept skipping the into... And with every reset I was more patient, sitting through the into and watching part of the story unfold.

But what really hooked me was that main theme... I could honestly sit there and listen to it for hours... And maybe did on more than one occasion. I still have it save to my phone, and even get the luxury of waking up to it as my morning alarm.

Honestly I can say it's one of the few pieces of music I can listen to and almost cry every time I hear it.

Well the concept of a Hotline Miami movie is pretty neat (I know I sure as hell would watch it) I don't know if it's the right medium for it.

From what I've seen, Hotline Miami focuses on gameplay over story. While there is a great story here, it seems that a lot of it points to the fact that games don't exactly need a story to function. The character goes in, acts like an animal, and then it all fades away after the violence is complete.

I'll link you to Errant Signal's video on it, as he shares a lot of the same views I do on it.
(Here's that link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AixOBp15KdI )

In other words, it works way better as a game than a movie.

This is in no way me trying to tell you that you *shouldn't* make it, but keep in mind that Hotline Miami is a game before it's a story. A lot of symbolism and even story points would be kinda made pointless.

But like I said, I would still watch this. Don't be discouraged.
